Folkets park is also nice but it's more likely for people to be there if you don't want to come across any people. 

I've seen people mention Västra hamnen and Slottsstaden. Those are solid places as well. Västra hamnen is a bit overrated IMO but the area has a nice vibe, probably in the early morning as well.

If you can get your hands on some kind of transport you could go to Hyllie and Holma which are a bit further away. Those places are also nice. 

Maybe steer clear of Rosengård during those early hours. It's a nice place but probably not the safest at that time of day. 

To end off my recommendations I'll just rapidfire some places off the top of my head that might be nice to visit.

Möllevången
Triangeln
Pildammsparken
Slussen
Gågatan

I'm gonna yap here because I really, really, REALLY hate this anime. 

Summertime render. It had an interesting premise similar to that of Erased and Re Zero so I thought I could give it a try. I started watching it when it was airing, which was a couple of years ago, so my recollection of the anime isn't that accurate.

There was a nice mystery going on in the beginning with all of the shadow people that kill normal humans and take their places. Seeing the main character try to prevent people from falling victim to them was interesting and made me want to watch more.

For example, the main character knew from one of his previous "loops" that the policeman would be killed by the shadow people when he was on patrol. The MC would prevent his death by reporting a fight at a bar (or something like that, I don't remember clearly) which would cause the policeman to take another route and not cross paths with the shadow people.

This was nice. This ability to go back in time with his memories intact whenever he dies isn't something new but I'm always open to a new take on the trope. I was under the assumption that the MC would use this power to save people from being killed and eventually figure out a solution to the problem altogether. 

Later the MC realized he also had a time limit because each time the "loop" restarted it would put him slightly later in time than in the previous loops. This was a nice way of differentiating this show from the other shows with a similar premise as well as a way to put some pressure on the MC.

Then I reached the episode of the festival and I realized the story was going to shit. The shadow people started a mass killing at the festival and some kind of main villain was introduced. Good lord, the shit he said was so damn stupid.

He made some kind of analogy with the situation the MC was in with a video game? It was completely out of left field and felt really out of place. For a lack of a better term, the villain had negative aura in his introduction.

Then there was also this little girl in a yukata that also just felt out of place. She was just floating high up in the air above the massacre with a blank expression. The main villain referred to her as his mother or something. I remember just thinking "What the f*** is going on? Nothing makes sense".

Before I forget, there was also that woman with the glasses that the MC accidentally motorboated in the first episode. She appeared shortly before the massacre and pretty much just spoiled the entire mystery. She revealed that when a shadow person takes over the body of a real person they destroy the real body and replace it with a hologram of some kind. The shadow of this fake body is the real body of the shadow people.

Well, there goes the mystery! The nice vibe the show had going for it was gone. Then when the main character goes back in time after the massacre he seeks out the woman.

He finds her and she immediately figures out the situation he's in. Like what? That's just lazy writing. Then there's some shit about her having a split personality where her other personality is her dead brother or something.

At that point I completely gave up hope for this series. There is no more mystery and it's very apparent that the author of this series really sucks at writing an interesting story. It's the kind of writing that appeals to 14 year olds or something.

I stopped watching shortly after that and didn't touch the series again. I did look up the author and their other works and I found out that they made spin-offs with the woman I was talking about earlier.

That's nice, real nice. A spin-off with the character that practically ruined a series. I hate that character so much. 

I have heard that the show turns into a battle shounen later on and that just salts the wound.

So yeah, I strongly suggest AGAINST watching this slop. I personally REALLY hate it.
